children: Italian industrial output rose 0.7% in July from the previous month after a 1.1% drop in June, data showed on Thursday, registering a stronger rebound than expected and getting the third quarter off to a firm start.
A Reuters survey of 11 analysts had pointed to a 0.3% month-on-month rise in July.
June's data was revised down marginally from an originally reported -1.0%.
Despite the July pick-up, ISTAT's rolling three-month average showed that in the May-July period industrial output was still down 0.1% compared with February-April.
On a work day-adjusted year-on-year basis, output was flat in July, versus a forecast of a 0.6% decline.
The Italian economy held up better than many analysts expected in the first half of this year, with gross domestic product rising by 0.3% in the first quarter and 0.2% in the second.
Giorgia Meloni's government in April forecast full-year 2026 gross domestic product growth of 0.6%, but budget watchdog UPB last month issued a significantly more upbeat projection of 0.9%.
Economy Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti said on Sunday that 2026 growth could be close to 1%.
In 2025 Italy grew by 0.5%, a third straight year of sub-1% growth.
